pr_body:
This PR adds support for `recvmsg()` socket call. It also adds support for `IP_PKTINFO` and `IPV6_RECVPKTINFO` socket options. Tests for both of these features are also added.

Fixes #36415
pr_comments: Fixing the pktinfo tests so that we always catch if the control buffer is too small.

issue_context.title: Need access to destination ip from socket recv
issue_context.body:
Today there is no way to retrieve destination ip address while receiving a packet thru a socket.
This is particularly useful when the interface has multiple ip addresses (for instance multicast).

A possible solution, compliant with POSIX, would be a combination of **recvmsg** and **IP_PKTINFO** socket option but recvmsg is not implemented yet in Zephyr.
Another option would be to add a dedicated function, something like recvfromto(socket, buf, len, flags, src_addr, src_addrlen, dest_addr, dest_addrlen).
comments:
> A possible solution, compliant with POSIX, would be a combination of **recvmsg** and **IP_PKTINFO** socket option but recvmsg is not implemented yet in Zephyr.

IMHO this would be a better solution than adding a new and non-compliant function for this. Both functions would need to dig out the destination IP address anyway so it would not make sense to implement new function for this purpose.

> IMHO this would be a better solution than adding a new and non-compliant function for this. Both functions would need to dig out the destination IP address anyway so it would not make sense to implement new function for this purpose.

I totally agree, however this is also a bit harder to implement. Because recvmsg is more complex with all the msghdr / iovec / control ancillary structures.
So implementing something like recvfromto would probably be easier to do, and also recvfrom could be inlined to recvfromto with NULL src_addr, maybe leading to overall smaller code footprint.

review_comments: Shall we have an initial loop run over allocated `msg_iov` entries, to clear `iov_base` pointer? Right now, in case `msg_iovlen > 1` and let's say allocation for the first `msg_iov` entry fails, we still have remaining `iov_base` pointer copies from the original msghdr. This will cause trouble when we jump to fail handler (will try to release the memory we did not allocate here).

nit: No need to add space after cast.

Why not cast `context->options.recv_pktinfo` directly, w/o if statement?

There are now multiple get option functions in this file, they all follow this same pattern. I think we could create a generic function for these, but in separate PR. I can prepare one after this one is merged.
Shall `cmsg` be checked for NULL ptr? `CMSG_FIRSTHDR` will return NULL if `msg->msg_controllen < sizeof(struct cmsghdr)`

Should it also be checked if there is any remaining data on the rx queue before `continue`? Because right now, if the data available on the stream matched exactly `iov_len`, and there is more `msg_iov` available, we're getting back to `zsock_wait_data()`, potentially blocking while the function could return what was received so far.
When is it src and when is it dst address? It seems we only set this as a dst address on receive?
I copied the struct verbatim from the RFC. I think the struct can be used in other ways too (did not check this).
Shall `msg->msg_controllen` be verified to be large enough before copy?
